Resolves #21635

`codeql-analysis.yml` gains a `concurrency` group keyed on the pull request number. Only `synchronize` cancels, so a new head cancels the analysis of the head it replaced. A `reopened` run, `dev` pushes, scheduled runs and re-runs each get a group of their own and never cancel. File Size Guard is untouched, since it keeps no group on purpose (`#20064`).

Evidence: L2 (the group expression, parsed) → L4 required (AC-1 needs two consecutive pushes on one PR; AC-2's `dev` receipt exists only after merge). AC-1's L4 is this PR's own runs. Residual: AC-2, Residual-Owner: #21541.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | CI-observed on this PR: the second push (`79dd4df8dc`) cancelled the first head's CodeQL run, and its own run completed (both runs in Test Evidence). |
| AC-2 | By construction: `push`, `schedule` and re-runs are grouped by `github.run_id`, and `cancel-in-progress` holds only for `synchronize`. The `dev`-push receipt is Post-Merge Validation. |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. The second, empty commit exists only to produce AC-1's receipt; the squash drops it.

## Test Evidence
- AC-1: [run 44797089131](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44797089131) for head `92cdc92836` ended `cancelled` (Analyze and the extraction guard both cancelled) once the second push arrived. [Run 44797146255](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44797146255) for head `79dd4df8dc` ended `success`.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [x] The first `dev` push after merge runs its CodeQL analysis to completion, and no `dev` run shows as cancelled (Residual-Owner: #21541). Receipt: https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21541#issuecomment-7049589153

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge** (*GitHub Actions `1 running + 1 pending` slot ceiling under rapid double-reopen*):
  Because GitHub Actions allows at most one running and one pending run per concurrency group even when `cancel-in-progress` evaluates to `false`, closing and reopening a PR *twice* while its initial `opened` run is still executing on an unchanged SHA (`opened` running in `codeql-<PR>`, `reopened #1` pending in `codeql-<PR>`, `reopened #2` arriving before `opened` finishes) would displace `reopened #1` from the pending slot as `cancelled` on that same SHA. In practice, closing and reopening twice inside a ~2.5-minute CodeQL window on an unchanged commit is vanishingly rare (and a manual re-run takes `github.run_id`), whereas queueing a single `reopened` behind `opened` and letting a subsequent `synchronize` sweep both is the exact behavior we want—strictly non-blocking.
